payload.objective: Test whether animal meropenem PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation.

context_sources.main:/objective: Test whether animal meropenem PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation.
context_sources.main:/study/regimen: Partial, independent IV/SC regimens and dose-fractionation/humanized-regimen descriptions (SC007, SC009, SC010, SC014, SC020, SC021, SC022).
context_sources.main:/study/population: Mouse, rat, guinea pig, rabbit, beagle dog, rhesus and cynomolgus monkeys, pregnant monkeys, and later human validation (SC007, SC022, SC023, SC026).
context_sources.main:/study/system: Animal disposition and infection studies, with in-vitro binding, enzyme and MIC sources (SC007, SC009, SC018, SC019, SC024).
context_sources.main:/study/measurements: PK, binding, distribution/excretion, MIC and preclinical PD summaries (SC007, SC009, SC016, SC024).
context_sources.main:/study/methods: Planned animal PK modeling, human translation, Emax/Hill index comparison, independent validation and PTA simulation (SC030, SC032, SC034, SC037, SC038).
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/0/stateme: Meropenem is a known-drug test case with existing human PK intended for independent validation.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/1/stateme: The primary outcome is model feasibility, not a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/2/stateme: Meropenem is the sole test drug; imipenem/cilastatin, ertapenem and other source comparators must not substitute for it.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/3/stateme: The project follows the translational objective of Sou T et al., Model-Informed Drug Development for Antimicrobials: Translational PK and PK/PD Modeling to Predict an Efficacious Human Dose for Apramycin, Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics, 2021;109:1063-1073, https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.2104.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/4/stateme: Do not import the apramycin model or its parameters from SC004.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/5/stateme: Meropenem_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is the single animal and in-vitro data workbook; its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes rather than a ready-made modeling dataset. These are proposal-described resource roles, not findings from inspecting the workbook.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/6/stateme: Cross_species describes one study giving 20 mg/kg IV to mouse, rat, guinea pig, rabbit, beagle dog and rhesus monkey. It includes digitized mean plasma curves, PK parameters, urinary recovery, dose effects in mice and guinea pigs, tissue levels, renal DHP-I kinetics and serum binding, plus a second laboratory's plasma-binding table. Guinea pig occurs only on this sheet. Only the stated dosing component is supplied in this proposal description.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/7/stateme: Use Cross_species for the core between-species comparison.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/8/stateme: Mouse includes PK parameters and fitted dose-fractionation PD parameters for A. baumannii in a neutropenic thigh model; the proposal supplies a dose-fractionation description rather than a numerical schedule. See MI001.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/9/stateme: A separate Mouse study compares humanized regimens against ESBL E. coli and K. pneumoniae in renally impaired mice; the proposal describes the regimen type without its numerical schedule.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/10/statem: Mouse also includes population PK with ELF in a P. aeruginosa pneumonia model.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/11/statem: Mouse additionally contains text-only PK and binding information.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/12/statem: Use Mouse sources for PK and eligible PD analysis.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/13/statem: Rat includes plasma levels after single IV dosing and after daily IV dosing for 92 days; some means contain substituted detection-limit values. These are separate dosing descriptions, without numerical dose amounts in the proposal.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/14/statem: Rat separately includes 14C excretion and urinary metabolite profiles.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/15/statem: Rat includes PK, target attainment and survival in neutropenic septic rats sampled as whole blood.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/16/statem: Use Rat sources for systemic PK; survival must not be treated as a bacterial-burden endpoint.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/17/statem: Rabbit includes population PK with plasma and CSF compartments in a P. aeruginosa meningoencephalitis model; concentrations are available only as model parameters. Component eligibility is addressed by SC031 and MI002.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/18/statem: Rabbit also includes in-vitro plasma binding from a preprint.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/19/statem: Dog includes 14C and unlabelled PK at 120 mg/kg IV with the open-ring metabolite H-4295, tissue radioactivity and 14-day repeat dosing. The proposal does not specify the repeat-dose schedule or establish that its doses equal the stated PK dose.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/20/statem: A separate abstract-only Dog study reports IV and SC administration at 20 mg/kg; other dosing components are not stated in the proposal.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/21/statem: Monkey includes 14C PK and excretion at 300 mg/kg IV in cynomolgus monkeys. This is the stated dosing component, subject to MI003.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/22/statem: Monkey separately includes maternal and fetal plasma levels in pregnant monkeys; see MI003.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/23/statem: In_vitro_MIC contains EUCAST MIC distributions by organism from a 2009 snapshot, comparative MICs for the A. baumannii thigh isolates, and single-strain MICs stated in animal studies. See MI012 and MI013.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/24/statem: Use matched strain MICs for PD; a population MIC distribution cannot replace them. Distribution-based attainment is handled separately in SC038.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/25/statem: Human reference tables comprise label PK statements, a healthy-volunteer study, EUCAST summary PK and human rows removed from animal sources. Their availability and release conditions are owned by MI004.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/26/statem: Meropenem_project_proposal.docx defines the task: Animal to Human Translation of Meropenem, Feasibility study, Version 1.0 (draft), 9 October 2026.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/27/statem: AGENT_README.md is described as explaining package use and known gaps; its body has not been inspected in this transformation.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/28/statem: Planned data preparation splits mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs; checks provenance, units, dose histories, analytes, matrices, experimental units and missing fields; and identifies usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/29/statem: Planned animal PK work selects eligible systemic models for each species with usable data, evaluates fit and parameter identifiability, evaluates held-out prediction where design permits, and documents exclusion or exploratory use of summary-only, figure-only or radiolabel evidence. Component support is governed by SC031.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/30/statem: Add pulmonary or CSF components only where supported. For the rabbit model-parameter-only concentrations in SC018, assess whether they support a model component or only exploratory constraints.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/31/statem: Planned human translation uses supported animal models with body size, protein binding, renal elimination and justified physiological relationships. Compare scaling with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/32/statem: Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and fT>MIC with uncertainty under specified doses and infusion durations, then freeze the animal model, scaling and predictions. Access to human outcomes follows MI004; prediction conditions remain subject to MI007.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/33/statem: For eligible data, planned PK/PD analysis compares fT>MIC, fAUC/MIC and fCmax/MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression separately by organism and infection site. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that available data cannot determine a best index or target.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/34/statem: Give all three indices and both regression families in SC034 equal eligibility. Compare them on the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability while counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/35/statem: Keep stasis, 1-log and 2-log kill targets separate. A target from one organism, infection site or endpoint—thigh CFU, lung ELF, CSF or survival—cannot set another.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/36/statem: Planned human validation applies the frozen model to the doses and infusion conditions in SC026, compares predicted and observed plasma PK, and assesses other matrices separately when compatible data exist. Report bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/37/statem: After PK validation and PD qualification, planned PTA simulation uses a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, including infusion duration, to estimate attainment at each MIC. Process the MIC distribution and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty; deliver PTA tables/curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code. If required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/38/statem: Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Group means, published fitted parameters and digitized points are not individual animals; flag means containing substituted detection-limit values. Do not invent IDs, variability—including interindividual variability from group summaries—exposure-response links or missing measurements.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/39/statem: Keep routes; unchanged meropenem, H-4295 and total 14C; total versus unbound drug; and plasma, serum, whole blood, ELF, CSF, tissue fluid and tissue homogenate separate. Separate per-animal from per-kilogram parameters and neutropenic, renally impaired, septic, infected, pregnant and repeat-dose animals from healthy single-dose animals. In-vitro DHP-I kinetics are not PK. Every conversion or physiological bridge requires a recorded justification.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/40/statem: Reported bound-fraction alternatives are approximately 10%, 24% and 34% for mouse, and below 1%, 7.5% and 12% for dog. Their unresolved source conflicts are owned by MI005 and MI006.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/41/statem: Never average conflicting within-species binding sources; carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/42/statem: Humanized regimens were designed from human PK.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/43/statem: Published PD targets and conclusions must not set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings. Do not use humanized regimens to tune scaling, and do not let human outcomes tune the animal model or scaling. Freeze PD targets before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps; the other freezes are specified in SC033, SC037 and SC046. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/44/statem: The EUCAST distributions were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/45/statem: Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators and censored categories. Do not interpret the EUCAST distributions as resistance rates. Derive probabilities transparently, freeze the MIC distribution/input before its applicable validation or dose-simulation step, and never silently renormalize incomplete coverage.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/46/statem: Propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/47/statem: Do not equate a successful fit with predictive validation or human PK agreement with validation of antibacterial efficacy or safety.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/48/statem: Preserve failures and data gaps; save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results; obtain human review before fitting.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/impact: The feasibility of an eligible matched-record PD index comparison cannot be established from the proposal's fitted-parameter descriptions alone.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/why_it: The proposal explicitly states that no Mouse-sheet source gives per-regimen CFU tables. This is a source-reported limitation; attachment bodies remain NOT_SEARCHED.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/clarif: Assess what PD analyses the described sources can support, and document whether the missing response tables prevent the comparison in SC034–SC035.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/impact: Rabbit records cannot yet be assigned a supported component role or an exploratory-only role.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/why_it: The proposal requires the assessment in SC031 but does not report its outcome; attachments have not been assessed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/clarif: Evaluate the support supplied by SC018 and record the resulting eligibility decision under SC031.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/field: Monkey source animal counts and doses
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/impact: Animal-count interpretation and dose-linked use of Monkey records remain unresolved.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/why_it: The proposal reports within-source disagreement in animal counts and doses for the Monkey material. It does not reproduce the conflicting alternatives, and attachment bodies are NOT_SEARCHED.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/clarif: Retain the animal counts and doses as printed, locate their exact study contexts during authorized preparation, and record the unresolved alternatives without silently reconciling them.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/field: Human validation data availability and release
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/impact: Independent comparison with human observations must await the permitted release.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/why_it: Human validation data are not in the supplied package. The reference tables described in SC026 are held in a separate file and released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/clarif: At task 5, release the separate human reference file only after confirming the required freezes; do not access its outcomes earlier.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/impact: A single resolved mouse binding value cannot be used for free-exposure interpretation or translation.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/why_it: The proposal identifies conflicting mouse binding sources; the reported alternatives are preserved in SC041.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/clarif: Retain the source-specific alternatives and assess their applicability under SC042 without averaging them.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/impact: A single resolved dog binding value cannot be used for free-exposure interpretation or translation.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/why_it: The proposal identifies conflicting dog binding sources; the reported alternatives are preserved in SC041.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/clarif: Retain the source-specific alternatives and assess their applicability under SC042 without averaging them.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/field: Human PK prediction doses and infusion durations
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/impact: The prospective profiles and exposure metrics in SC033 cannot be defined for a concrete prediction setting.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/why_it: The proposal calls for specified doses and infusion durations but supplies no chosen human prediction values. This is proposal-bounded missingness, not a finding about unread reference files.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/clarif: Specify the prospective human PK prediction doses and infusion durations before generating and freezing the predictions.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/impact: Index selection cannot proceed under a registered decision rule.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/why_it: SC035 requires registration before fitting, but the proposal does not specify the selection rule.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/clarif: Prespecify and register the index-selection rule while retaining the comparison constraints in SC035.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/impact: Human prediction performance cannot receive a prespecified acceptance judgment.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/why_it: SC037 names performance measures but the proposal does not define the criteria against which they will be judged.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/clarif: Fix the human validation criteria before validation and bind them to the frozen prediction.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/impact: PTA simulation lacks its prespecified target-population definition.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/why_it: The population required by SC038 is not specified in the proposal.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/clarif: Prespecify the human population before PTA simulation, with any variability basis supported or explicitly limited as required by MI014.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/impac: PTA cannot be calculated for defined regimens or infusion-duration scenarios.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/why_i: SC038 requires prespecified dosing scenarios including infusion duration, but the proposal gives no scenario choices.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/clari: Prespecify the human PTA dosing scenarios and infusion durations before simulation.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/impac: The denominator basis for deriving MIC probabilities requires explicit resolution.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/why_i: The proposal explicitly states that the EUCAST distributions carry no totals; this source-reported gap is not an attachment inspection result.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/clari: Establish and document a defensible denominator basis from authorized inputs, or retain the resulting limitation on distribution-weighted attainment.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/field: MIC coverage assessment and probability handling
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/impac: A transparent MIC probability distribution cannot yet be frozen for weighted attainment.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/why_i: The proposal does not assess coverage or specify treatment of any incomplete coverage. Its prohibition in SC046 does not establish that coverage is actually incomplete.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/clari: Assess MIC coverage and record probability handling, preserving censored categories and any unresolved limitation under SC046.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/impac: A defensible individual-variability basis for subsequent population predictions has not been established.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/why_i: The proposal describes summary-level evidence and prohibits invented variability, but does not establish whether defensible individual PK variability can be supported. Attachment bodies remain NOT_SEARCHED.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/clari: Assess the available experimental units and variability evidence during PK work; record supported variability or the resulting limitation without manufacturing it from group summaries.

project_rules.text: R01: Use meropenem as the sole test drug; comparators in the sources are not substitutes. Do not import the apramycin model or its parameters.

evidence.quote: Meropenem is the sole test drug; imipenem/cilastatin, ertapenem and other comparators that appear in the sources are not substitutes.
Following the translational objective of Sou et al. (2021), we do not import the apramycin model or its parameters.

project_rules.text: R02: Use Meropenem_source_tables_by_species.xlsx as the single animal and in-vitro data workbook. Split its mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs. Check provenance, units, dose histories, analytes, matrices, experimental units and missing fields, and identify usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.

evidence.quote: Meropenem_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is the single animal and in-vitro data workbook. Its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes, not a ready-made modeling dataset:

1. Prepare the data. Split the mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs. Check provenance, units, dose histories, analytes, matrices, experimental units and missing fields. Identify usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.

project_rules.text: R03: Use Cross_species for the core between-species comparison, Mouse for PK and eligible PD analysis, and Rat for systemic PK. Do not treat rat survival as a bacterial-burden endpoint. Assess whether rabbit concentrations available only as model parameters support a model component or only exploratory constraints.

evidence.quote: Use for the core between-species comparison; the guinea pig appears only here.
Use for PK and eligible PD analysis; no source gives per-regimen CFU tables.
Use for systemic PK; survival is not a bacterial-burden endpoint.
Concentrations are available only as model parameters; assess whether they support a model component or only exploratory constraints.

project_rules.text: R04: Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Do not treat group means, published fitted parameters or digitized points as individual animals. Flag means containing substituted detection-limit values. Do not invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links or missing measurements. Keep conflicting monkey animal counts and doses as printed.

evidence.quote: 1. Preserve evidence level. Keep source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Group means, published fitted parameters and digitized points are not individual animals. Flag means that contain substituted detection-limit values. Do not invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links or missing measurements.
Animal counts and doses disagree within the source; keep them as printed.

project_rules.text: R05: Separate routes; unchanged meropenem, H-4295 and total 14C; total and unbound drug; and plasma, serum, whole blood, ELF, CSF, tissue fluid and tissue homogenate. Keep per-animal and per-kilogram parameters apart. Keep neutropenic, renally impaired, septic, infected, pregnant and repeat-dose animals apart from healthy single-dose animals. Do not treat in vitro DHP-I kinetics as PK. Record a justification for every conversion or physiological bridge.

evidence.quote: 2. Keep biological quantities compatible. Separate routes, analytes (unchanged meropenem, H-4295, total 14C), total versus unbound drug, and plasma, serum, whole blood, ELF, CSF, tissue fluid and tissue homogenate. Keep per-animal and per-kilogram parameters apart, and keep neutropenic, renally impaired, septic, infected, pregnant and repeat-dose animals apart from healthy single-dose animals. In vitro DHP-I kinetics are not PK. Every conversion or physiological bridge requires a recorded justification.

project_rules.text: R06: Never average conflicting within-species binding sources; carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

evidence.quote: Binding sources conflict within species (for example mouse about 10% versus 24% versus 34% bound; dog below 1% versus 7.5% versus 12%); never average them, and carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

project_rules.text: R07: Obtain human review before fitting.

evidence.quote: Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results, and obtain human review before fitting.

project_rules.text: R10: Release the separate human reference tables only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen. Human outcomes cannot tune the animal model or scaling. Do not use humanized regimens to tune scaling because they were designed from human PK.

evidence.quote: Human validation data are not in this package. Human reference tables (label PK statements, a healthy-volunteer study, EUCAST summary PK, and human rows removed from the animal sources) are held in a separate file and released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
Humanized regimens were designed from human PK; do not use them to tune scaling. Human outcomes cannot tune the animal model or scaling.

project_rules.text: R11: Use matched strain MICs for PD and MIC distributions for population-weighted attainment. A distribution cannot replace matched strain MICs.

evidence.quote: Use matched strain MICs for PD and the distributions for population-weighted attainment; a distribution cannot replace matched strain MICs.

project_rules.text: R18: Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators and censored categories. Do not interpret the EUCAST distributions, which carry no totals and were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs, as resistance rates. Derive probabilities transparently, freeze the MIC distribution and never silently renormalize incomplete coverage. Distinguish per-MIC PTA from MIC-weighted attainment.

evidence.quote: 5. Process MIC and PTA explicitly. Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators and censored categories. The EUCAST distributions carry no totals and were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs; do not read them as resistance rates. Derive probabilities transparently and freeze the MIC distribution; never silently renormalize incomplete coverage. Distinguish per-MIC PTA from MIC-weighted attainment.

project_rules.text: R21: Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results.

evidence.quote: Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results, and obtain human review before fitting.

project_rules.text: R08: Select eligible systemic PK models for each species with usable data, adding pulmonary or CSF components only where supported. Evaluate fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits. Document exclusion or exploratory use of summary-only, figure-only or radiolabel evidence.

evidence.quote: 2. Fit animal PK. Select eligible systemic PK models for each species with usable data, and add pulmonary or CSF components only where supported. Evaluate fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits. Document exclusion or exploratory use of summary-only, figure-only or radiolabel evidence.

project_rules.text: R09: Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, renal elimination and justified physiological relationships. Compare scaling with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better. Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and fT>MIC with uncertainty under specified doses and infusion durations, and freeze the predictions before opening human outcomes.

evidence.quote: 3. Predict human PK. Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, renal elimination and justified physiological relationships. Compare scaling with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better. Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and fT>MIC with uncertainty under specified doses and infusion durations, and freeze them before opening human outcomes.

project_rules.text: R15: Freeze the model, validation criteria, PD targets and MIC input before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.

evidence.quote: Freeze the model, validation criteria, PD targets and MIC input before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.

project_rules.text: R12: For eligible data, give fT>MIC, fAUC/MIC and fCmax/MIC equal eligibility and compare all three using both ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression, separately by organism and infection site. Use the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that the available data cannot determine a best index or target.

evidence.quote: 4. Determine the PK/PD index. For eligible data, compare fT>MIC, fAUC/MIC and fCmax/MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression, separately by organism and infection site. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that the available data cannot determine a best index or target.

3. Give all three indices equal eligibility and both regression families. Compare them on the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability, counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner.

project_rules.text: R13: Keep stasis, 1-log and 2-log kill targets separate. A target from one organism, infection site or endpoint, including thigh CFU, lung ELF, CSF or survival, cannot set another.

evidence.quote: Keep stasis, 1-log and 2-log kill targets separate; a target from one organism, infection site or endpoint (thigh CFU, lung ELF, CSF, survival) cannot set another.

project_rules.text: R14: Published PD targets and conclusions in the sources cannot set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings.

evidence.quote: Published PD targets and conclusions in the sources cannot set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings.

project_rules.text: R17: After PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, including infusion duration, to estimate PTA at each MIC. Process the MIC distribution and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty. Deliver PTA tables or curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

evidence.quote: 6. Produce PTA and assess feasibility. After PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, including infusion duration, to estimate the probability of target attainment (PTA) at each MIC. Process the MIC distribution and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty. Deliver the PTA tables/curves, feasibility conclusion and reproducible code; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

project_rules.text: R20: Report model feasibility as the primary outcome, without presenting it as a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability. A successful fit is not predictive validation, and human PK agreement does not validate antibacterial efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps.

evidence.quote: The primary outcome is model feasibility, not a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability.
6. Limit and document conclusions. A successful fit is not predictive validation; human PK agreement does not validate antibacterial efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps.

library.interpretation: These profiles are project-designed summaries informed by the cited sources, not verbatim guidance or universal regulatory requirements. Use only assigned profiles and assess applicability against the project objective and published rules. Profiles marked DATA_REQUIREMENTS_ONLY report source-backed input coverage and gaps; they do not select analytical methods or qualify results. Prior analytical guidance is retained separately for downstream review and is not loaded into this stage. A profile cannot authorize source access, publish project rules, approve an analysis or impose an unreviewed numeric cutoff. No historical assessment or approval is refreshed automatically. data_roles and condition_triggers let host code map DC labels onto the conditions of profiles already selected from the objective; data never select a profile. A trigger with review OBJECTIVE or DATA, or an undecided label, leaves applicability to the independent coverage review.

sources.title: ICH M15: General Principles for Model-Informed Drug Development
sources.supports: Question-specific intended use, criteria, assumptions and fit-for-purpose evaluation; no fixed species-count rule is imported.

sources.title: Phoenix: Lambda Z or Slope Estimation settings
sources.locator: Limitations of Lambda Z and slope estimation
sources.supports: Parameters independent of terminal slope remain reportable when slope estimation fails. Software point-count settings are not universal scientific sufficiency criteria.

sources.title: Phoenix: NCA parameter formulas
sources.locator: Discrete plasma parameters; extrapolation; extravascular clearance/volume footnote
sources.supports: Endpoint-specific input dependencies and distinction between absolute parameters and apparent parameters containing F.

sources.title: Bailer (1988): Testing for the equality of area under the curves when using destructive measurement techniques
sources.supports: Group-level AUC estimation under destructive sampling; not reconstruction of individual trajectories.

sources.title: Tang et al. (2007): Interspecies prediction of human drug clearance based on scaling data from one or two animal species
sources.supports: Calibrated one-/two-species approaches have method-specific evidence. This does not authorize arbitrary fixed exponents or make a species count a validation result.

sources.title: Ring et al. (2011): PhRMA CPCDC initiative, part 3: prediction methods of human clearance
sources.supports: Allometry and IVIVE require different inputs and binding conventions. IV CL comparison involved 19 drugs; applicability to a new drug remains to be assessed.

sources.title: EMA: Use of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in development of antimicrobial medicinal products
sources.locator: Nonclinical PK-PD studies; PK-PD targets and target attainment
sources.supports: Antimicrobial exposure, susceptibility and effect must be linked for the intended use; in vitro and animal infection models can contribute complementary evidence.

sources.title: Bakker-Woudenberg IAJM, ten Kate MT, Goessens WHF, Mouton JW (2006): Effect of treatment duration on pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic indices correlating with therapeutic efficacy of ceftazidime in experimental Klebsiella pneumoniae lung infection
sources.supports: Index conclusions depend on treatment duration and the response endpoint; the rat-model design varied total dose and dosing interval (every 6, 12 or 24 h). Do not transplant the study's winning index or numeric target into another project.

sources.title: Phoenix: PK model options
sources.supports: Compartmental representations require structural and dosing parameters; choosing parameterization is an explicit modeling decision.

sources.title: Heinzl (1996): A note on testing areas under the curve when using destructive measurement techniques
sources.supports: Mean-curve AUC and its variance depend on sampling design and available summaries. The paper corrects an earlier testing approximation; no inferential procedure is automatically adopted by this profile.

sources.title: PKNCA: AUC integration methods
sources.locator: Integration before Tlast; AUClast, AUCall and AUCinf definitions
sources.supports: Integration and extrapolation choices are explicit settings. Package defaults are not project approval or universal requirements.

sources.title: PKNCA: Handle BLQ values in concentration measurements
sources.locator: Details: missing-value handling and first, middle and last BLQ values
sources.supports: Missingness and BLQ handling interact with curve position and require specification. Package input encoding does not authorize overwriting original censoring information.

sources.title: Phoenix: Sparse sampling (pre-clinical) data
sources.locator: Mean Curve Final Parameters and SE_AUClast/SE_AUCall limitations
sources.supports: Mean-curve parameters have a group-level estimand. The documented sparse-AUC standard-error method depends on a linear combination of means and is not automatically applicable to logarithmic trapezoids.

sources.title: Cheng and Jusko (1988): Mean Residence Time Concepts for Pharmacokinetic Systems with Nonlinear Drug Elimination Described by the Michaelis-Menten Equation
sources.supports: For the studied Michaelis-Menten systems, Dose/AUC is a time-average clearance and AUMC/AUC differs from true MRT. This supports an applicability check, not a prohibition on descriptive AUC under all nonlinear conditions.

sources.title: Lee et al. (2021): Pharmacokinetic Characterization of LW6, a Novel Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha) Inhibitor in Mice
sources.supports: Metabolite exposure after parent dosing was distinguished from disposition after direct metabolite dosing. Formation calculations used analyte-specific clearance and molecular-weight conversion. No drug-specific parameter is transferred.

sources.title: Phoenix: NCA Object
sources.locator: Dose types for models 200-202 and steady-state assumptions
sources.supports: The relevant infusion model assumes constant input. Together with the NCA formulas this bounds the Tinf/2 correction; interrupted or varying input requires separate treatment.

sources.title: Phoenix: Sparse sampling calculation
sources.locator: Mean concentration at unique times; nominal-time recommendation; repeated-sample correlation
sources.supports: Time handling must match sampling design. Nominal-time grouping for a sparse procedure differs from individual actual times; the software recommendation is not a universal substitution rule.

sources.title: ICH M10: Bioanalytical Method Validation and Study Sample Analysis
sources.supports: Reported concentrations depend on a defined assay, matrix, calibration range and LLOQ, with stability and recovery assessed. The profile records whether this information exists; it does not grade an assay.

sources.title: PKNCA: Secondary parameters (renal clearance)
sources.locator: Renal clearance, start to finish; Units that differ between the two profiles
sources.supports: Renal clearance links the amount excreted in a urine collection (concentration and volume over start-end times) to plasma AUC over the same interval. Package settings are not project approval.

profiles.name: Data requirements for observed peaks and finite-window NCA
profiles.applies_when: The project requests observed peak summaries or finite-window exposure. Check input definitions, permitted source data and sampling coverage separately for each endpoint. Numerical NCA methods and result evaluation belong to the later analysis module.
required_inputs: Each requested endpoint and intended use; proposal-defined AUC window and time origin, with analyte, matrix and total/free concentration basis.
Permitted concentration-time data with units, study/profile membership and dosing context.
Source origin, data level and sampling design: original versus digitized data; individual versus group summary; serial, destructive or mixed sampling.
conditional_inputs: Dose amount and dose basis when the objective requires normalization or comparison; dosing times and single-dose, repeated-dose or verified steady-state context where they define the window.

For digitized observations: the source figure, panel/curve, axes and transformations, units, extraction provenance and any existing reconstruction review. Distinguish measured points from fitted or predicted curves.

For group summaries: arithmetic/geometric mean or median, contributing sample counts and reported SD/SE/CI definitions; variance/covariance information if uncertainty is requested. Missing uncertainty information is distinct from missing point-estimate inputs.
BLQ/LLOQ, missing-value flags and actual versus nominal time definitions where relevant. If these are unspecified, retain the ambiguity.

Bioanalytical context where reported: assay method, measured matrix (plasma, serum or blood), calibration range and LLOQ, validation status, and any reported stability, recovery or adsorption problem. Record whether this information exists; do not grade the assay.

For site-of-infection or tissue matrices: sampling method, any dilution correction (for example urea-based correction of lavage fluid), tissue mass or volume basis and units. Keep these concentrations separate from plasma or serum concentrations.
acceptable_alternatives: Digitized measured group means may be candidate data for group-level NCA. Preserve their provenance and limitations; do not manufacture individual observations.

Record available evidence or an existing reviewed plan for unobserved boundaries. If resolution requires an analytical method, mark it for the NCA module rather than selecting or testing that method here.
data_checks: Match available data to every requested endpoint. Do not infer coverage from filenames, headers, row count or the availability of another endpoint.

Require the proposal to define each AUC window by intended use, including AUCtau when relevant. Retain an undefined window as an unresolved definition; do not choose 0-24 h, infinity or a shorter observed interval by default.

List observed times, window boundaries and internal unsampled intervals. Distinguish observed, source-reported estimated and unobserved boundary values. Do not fill gaps or select integration or boundary-treatment methods.
Keep studies, regimens, matrices, individual records and group-summary curves distinct. Do not interchange arithmetic means, geometric means and medians.
Observed Cmax/Tmax refer to sampled concentrations. A group-mean curve does not establish the unobserved true peak or the mean of individual peaks.
Retain BLQ and missingness without substitution. Report unavailable uncertainty inputs separately from unavailable inputs for a point estimate.

Check that the dose basis and the measured analyte correspond: salt versus free base, mass versus activity units, and, for multi-component substances, which components the dose and the assay each refer to. A conversion factor needs a cited source; retain an unresolved basis rather than converting.

Identify the time-zero condition implied by route and input: an unobserved initial concentration after bolus dosing, the end of infusion for infusions, and pre-dose concentrations for repeated dosing. Record whether each boundary value is observed, source-assumed or unknown; leave any back-extrapolation to the NCA module.
profiles.missing_effect: Report input coverage and gaps for each requested endpoint. A missing definition or unresolved coverage prevents declaring its input requirements met; retain independent supported input matches and route method-dependent questions to NCA analysis.
not_established: Completed NCA, reliable numerical exposure or an approved integration/boundary method.
Individual trajectories, individual variability or uncertainty reconstructed from group means.
A universal sampling-count threshold or permission to replace the requested endpoint.
outputs: Endpoint-specific input requirement and matched source evidence
Input availability status, limitations and unresolved definitions
Missing material, affected task or endpoint, required phase and next action

profiles.name: Data requirements for terminal-dependent NCA endpoints
target_endpoints: terminal extrapolated area within a specified finite window
AUMC and MRT when explicitly requested
profiles.applies_when: A requested endpoint needs terminal-phase information. Inherit the relevant MP001 input requirements and inspect available late-time data. Terminal-interval selection, regression and extrapolation are deferred to NCA analysis.
required_inputs: The requested endpoint, window or extrapolation extent, time origin and data-level definitions, retaining unresolved MP001 inputs.
Late concentration-time observations with source membership, units, quantifiability and reported BLQ/LLOQ information.
Dosing times and infusion duration or history needed to interpret the late observations in relation to ongoing or subsequent input.
conditional_inputs: Available absorption/input information for extravascular dosing when needed to interpret late observations.
Replicate counts and reported uncertainty, variance or covariance information if uncertainty is a requested output.
For MRT or Vss, retain the additional time/input information required by MP003. Data available for AUC alone do not establish all moment-dependent input requirements.
acceptable_alternatives: Original numerical data or traceable digitized measured observations may be candidates at their actual data level.
Keep independently supported MP001 input matches when terminal-dependent inputs are incomplete; do not substitute their endpoints for the original target.
data_checks: Inventory late sample times, concentrations, quantifiable observations, gaps and known dosing/input events. Do not declare the last few observations a valid terminal phase merely because they are last.
Check whether endpoint and timing definitions are explicit and compatible with the source records. Do not silently change the requested exposure window.

Identify absent late data or unresolved absorption, dosing and quantifiability information. If sufficiency requires a fitted slope or extrapolation diagnostic, report it as unresolved for downstream analysis.
Assess available inputs separately for each terminal-dependent endpoint without imposing a universal point count or calculating regression, residuals or tail fractions.
profiles.missing_effect: Identify affected terminal-dependent endpoints and the missing data or definition. Input availability permits further assessment only; the current step cannot certify a usable terminal estimate. Preserve independent finite-window data matches.
not_established: A selected terminal interval, fitted lambda_z, calculated tail contribution or accepted terminal estimate.
An elimination mechanism, individual parameter distribution or human predictive validity.
outputs: Endpoint-specific input requirement and matched source evidence
Input availability status, limitations and unresolved definitions
Missing material, affected task or endpoint, required phase and next action

profiles.name: Data requirements for animal CL and Vss
target_endpoints: explicitly requested apparent parameters such as CL/F
profiles.applies_when: The objective requests animal disposition parameters. Inspect the data or permitted reported estimates available for each parameter. Do not calculate parameters, qualify results or count qualified species in this step.
required_inputs: The exact requested parameter and intended use, distinguishing CL from CL/F and Vss from Vz, Vc and apparent volumes.
Permitted concentration-time data and applicable MP001/MP002 input metadata, or a traceable permitted same-drug published estimate retained as a literature candidate.
Route, analyte-specific dose and dose basis, dosing times, regimen, units, biological matrix, total/free basis and actual data level.
conditional_inputs: For single-dose IV clearance, data covering the exposure course including late observations relevant to AUCinf. For a steady-state interval approach, evidence of steady state and a proposal-defined interval with matching dose and exposure data.

For Vss, time-course data potentially supporting the required exposure/moment information and the dosing-input history; infusion duration and whether input was constant, varying or interrupted. Single-dose data are not excluded solely because the parameter name contains steady state.
A source-supported applicable bioavailability estimate if absolute CL is requested from extravascular evidence; otherwise retain the distinction from CL/F.
Formation/systemic-input information and active-moiety or molecular-weight basis when the measured analyte is formed from the administered parent/prodrug.
Body weight when dose/parameter normalization or later scaling requires it; relevant dose-dependence information and reported uncertainty where available or required by the objective.

Characteristics of the contributing animals as reported: species, strain, sex, actual body weight, and health, infection or renal-function state. Record unreported characteristics as gaps; do not assume healthy or typical animals.
acceptable_alternatives: NCA input data or published estimates may be candidates without a compartmental fit. This does not qualify the resulting parameter for extrapolation.

When project permissions allow, same-drug published CL/Vss without original curves may enter as LITERATURE_REPORTED, NOT_RECALCULATED and NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED. Retain citation/page/table, parameter definition, study/dose context, estimation method, reported uncertainty and missing information.

A group-summary point estimate without reliable uncertainty remains a candidate with an explicit uncertainty gap. Preserve the required later human use review; do not count it as a qualified species here.
data_checks: Map inputs separately to CL and Vss; availability for one does not establish availability for the other. An available finite-window AUC does not automatically meet a request requiring exposure to infinity.
Check route, analyte input, matrix, free/total basis, weight normalization and units against the requested parameter. Do not merge incompatible definitions.
Check whether dose refers to the measured analyte or its parent/prodrug. Missing formation information may leave absolute analyte clearance unresolved while exposure data remain usable.
Preserve group-level parameter meaning, reported dose dependence and unresolved input-history information. Do not choose or test a clearance, moment or infusion-correction formula.

For a literature-only candidate, identify what is actually reported and what cannot be independently checked without underlying data. Candidate registration is not parameter validation or species qualification.
Apply the MP001 dose-basis and analyte-composition check to every dose used for a requested parameter. An unresolved basis leaves the dose-dependent inputs for that parameter unresolved.
Map Vz separately from CL and Vss: it depends on the terminal-phase inputs assessed under MP002.
profiles.missing_effect: Record which input or definition is missing for each parameter, its intended use and the required next action. Retain available candidates and independent input matches; parameter qualification and the project-specific species minimum are assessed later.
not_established: Calculated or accepted CL/Vss, a compartmental curve shape, or qualification for human extrapolation.
Absolute clearance from an extravascular dose without applicable F, or interchangeability of Vss, Vz and Vc.
A known uncertainty distribution merely because a candidate was registered or reviewed.
outputs: Endpoint-specific input requirement and matched source evidence
Input availability status, limitations and unresolved definitions
Missing material, affected task or endpoint, required phase and next action

profiles.name: Data requirements for urinary excretion and renal clearance
target_endpoints: Amount and fraction of dose excreted unchanged in urine (Ae, fe)
Nonrenal clearance by difference when explicitly requested
outputs: Endpoint-specific input requirement and matched source evidence
Input availability status, limitations and unresolved definitions
Missing material, affected task or endpoint, required phase and next action
profiles.applies_when: The project requests urinary excretion, renal clearance or a renal/nonrenal split of clearance. Reuse the MP001 and MP003 definitions for plasma exposure, dose basis and analyte; inspect only urine-specific inputs. Calculation belongs to the later analysis module.
required_inputs: Urine collection intervals with start and end times relative to dosing, and whether collection was complete for each interval.
For each interval: urine volume and analyte concentration with units, or a reported amount excreted; the analyte and its relation to the administered dose basis.
The dose, route and dose basis that fe refers to.
conditional_inputs: Plasma exposure over the same intervals when renal clearance is requested, assessed under MP001 and MP003.
Total clearance from MP003 when nonrenal clearance by difference is requested.
Metabolite or conjugate measurements in urine when the objective separates unchanged drug from metabolites.
acceptable_alternatives: Published same-drug fe or CLR may enter as LITERATURE_REPORTED, NOT_RECALCULATED and NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VALIDATED when project permissions allow, with source, definition, collection duration and missing information.
data_checks: Distinguish concentrations from amounts and cumulative from interval values. Do not derive an amount without a recorded volume.
Compare the collection duration with the requested endpoint. Excretion up to the last collection is not total excretion; do not extrapolate it here.
Check that plasma and urine intervals, analytes and units correspond before matching them to renal clearance. Keep unresolved correspondence as a gap.
Record missing, pooled or incomplete collections and the experimental unit (individual animal or pooled cage) without inventing animal IDs.
profiles.missing_effect: Report the affected excretion or clearance endpoint and its missing urine input through the general data-gap policy. Missing urine data do not block plasma-based PK work.
not_established: Calculated fe, CLR or nonrenal clearance.
Complete excretion from a truncated collection, or an elimination mechanism.

profiles.name: Data requirements for animal PK modeling
target_endpoints: animal PK parameters requested by the project
profiles.applies_when: The objective requests an animal time-course model. Check the available modeling inputs and unresolved design information. Model selection, fitting and result evaluation belong to the animal PK module.
required_inputs: Requested modeling objective, parameter or curve outputs and intended use.
Permitted concentration-time observations, dosing events, route, analyte, matrix, concentration basis and units.
Study/regimen membership, sampling design, data level and available experimental-unit identifiers; identify unverifiable IDs rather than inventing them.
conditional_inputs: Infusion duration/input history, extravascular dosing information, or covariates such as body weight when required by the stated objective.
Verified individual-level records and sampling structure when individual or population variability is requested. Do not impose dense repeated sampling for every animal as a universal input rule.
Summary definition, counts and reported variability for group-summary curves; source extraction details for digitized observations; BLQ/LLOQ and missingness metadata where relevant.
Concentration-time data at more than one dose level when the objective includes characterizing dose-dependent (nonlinear) kinetics. Do not impose a number of dose levels.
acceptable_alternatives: Measured group-mean curves may be candidate inputs for exploratory group-level modeling with stated limitations, without inferred animal random effects.
Keep data potentially supporting a separate NCA objective available when modeling inputs are incomplete; do not replace the requested modeling objective silently.
data_checks: Map available concentration, timing, dose, route and grouping information to the stated modeling objective. Report actual coverage and missing phases or dose levels without a universal row-count threshold.
Distinguish individual records, destructive sampling and group summaries. Unverified cross-time IDs do not establish individual trajectories.
Keep study and regimen identities. Identify compatibility questions for later model design; do not pool incompatible sources or treat every source curve as a separate mandatory model.

If input sufficiency depends on a structural model or numerical assessment, retain the uncertainty for the animal PK module. Do not choose compartments, error models, estimation engines or diagnostic thresholds here.
profiles.missing_effect: Report available modeling inputs, task-specific gaps and the data or clarification needed. A positive input assessment permits the next preparation/design step only and does not approve fitting or its results.
not_established: An accepted structural model, convergence, parameter identifiability, uncertainty or a valid human prediction.
Animal IIV from group means or unverified IDs.
Automatic preference for additional compartments or a completed model comparison.
